summary: Frontend E2E testing of Centralized Payroll Voucher Submission & Approval System — passed all critical flows on gov tenant + superadmin/enterprise regression. Full 4-eyes workflow (draft → pending_supervisor → submitted → under_review → approved → payment_authorized), return-for-correction with revision tracking, immutability post-authorization, segregation-of-duties + dual-control fraud guards, branch CRUD, manual voucher creation, users-page finance flag pill/toggle, plain-employee scoping — all verified via Playwright.
action_items: MINOR/UX: The 'New voucher' (voucher-new) button is rendered for plain employees who are NOT branch supervisors. When Joseph (plain employee) clicks it, the branch dropdown (vc-branch) has only the placeholder because myBranches filter yields []. Consider hiding voucher-new when canManage=false and user is not a supervisor of any branch, or showing an empty-state message instead of an unusable modal.

OBSERVATION (not a blocker): Generate-from-run modal on gov tenant showed 0 selectable runs — /payroll/runs likely returned empty for the current filter/context even though the dashboard shows LAST RUN NET SLE 50,760.05 for 2026-10. Worth a quick check that generate-from-run has usable runs available on gov tenant, or verify the seeder creates at least one gov payroll run to exercise this modal end-to-end.

OBSERVATION: Joseph (described as 'plain employee, no flags, not a supervisor') sees 'Pending Leaves 3 — Awaiting your approval' on dashboard, implying she is treated as an approver somewhere. Unrelated to vouchers feature but worth verifying seed data.
critical_code_review_comments: Vouchers.jsx line 84: <button data-testid='voucher-new'> is always rendered regardless of role. Since CreateVoucherModal only shows supervisor branches for non-manage users, this is at minimum a UX papercut for plain employees.
VoucherDetail.jsx supervisor-approve visibility (line 232): correctly falls back to isAdminRole so admins can act for supervisors when the branch supervisor is unavailable — matches spec.
Segregation-of-duties + dual-control checks (lines 246-267) use v.created_by/approved_by string equality against user email — works consistently in testing.
Return-for-correction confirm button correctly disabled until reason.trim().length >= 10 — verified in UI.
